title: Where am I? Position embeddings
summary: Why the model needs a second table, and what happens without it.

steps.text: Attention, on its own, treats its input as a set: it cannot tell “ab” from “ba”. So each position also gets a learned vector from the **position table** `wpe`, added to the token's vector.
steps.prompt: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She

steps.text: This heatmap has one row per position, and it is the same for every prompt: it depends only on where a token is, never on which token is there. Smooth changes from row to row are the model's sense of distance.

ask.question: Open the sum of the two, `x₀ = tok + pos`, in the pipeline map on the left.
ask.hint: It is the first node on the spine, with a ⊕.
ask.correct: This is the residual stream's starting point: what each position knows before any layer runs.

steps.text: Now an experiment: shuffle the position embeddings, so every token is told the wrong position. Watch the next-token panel on the right, and the loss in the interventions tab.
The predictions fall apart: the model has lost track of order. Clearing the intervention restores them.
